about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Luis Obispo, California
about.longDescription: San Luis Obispo sees steady traffic on corridors like US-101 Southbound, Los Osos Valley Road, Broad Street, and Higuera Street — and public records show 179 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, hurting 223 people and claiming 1 life. Crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., when commuters, students, and weekend travelers all converge downtown and along the highway. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in a slip-and-fall, workplace accident, or dog bite anywhere in the county, you deserve straightforward answers about your options. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm. We simply connect injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened and explain what California law allows. There's no cost to talk, no obligation to hire anyone, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of understanding where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity — like a city road crew — can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on compensation entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your share is assessed fairly.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases. That means your recovery isn't artificially limited the way it is in some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you win. That removes the financial barrier to finding out whether you have a valid claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in San Luis Obispo?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity — such as a city street department — the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's wise to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in San Luis Obispo?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors like US-101 Southbound, Los Osos Valley Road, Broad Street, and Higuera Street, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. This is different from some other states that impose such limits.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay nothing unless they recover compensation for you.
